OCCVM — the reference surface

One live specimen per law, drawn from the spine parts spliced into this file. Not a gallery of intentions: if a value here is wrong, the spine is wrong, because this page holds no values of its own.

READ THIS FIRST

What this page can and cannot tell you

It can tell you what the spine currently resolves to, on this browser, at this instant, at this place — every token below is read off the live document rather than transcribed. If a part is unspliced or a token renamed, this page degrades visibly instead of quietly rendering something plausible, because it authors no fallback colour of its own.

It cannot tell you that a tool conforms. A tool's conformance is decided by test/occvm.js, the unit suites and the golden set — assertions that run, not a page a person looks at. This surface is the eye's instrument beside those: it makes a drift visible, and it is recorded into the golden set as a third surface so that a change in the spine itself shows up here even when neither tool happens to reveal it.

OCCVM-L1

Substrate and inscription

Obsidian substrate, bone inscription. --bone-lo is derived from --bone — carried a quarter of the way to --edge — so the pair cannot separate again as the light moves.

OCCVM-L2

Cut geometry

A surface is cut, not rounded: radius ≤ 4px, and the bevel is struck from the light rather than from a fixed edge. Both slabs below are the spine's own .occvm-slab primitive; the bevel on each turns with --lx/--ly through the day.

.occvm-slab
radius 4px — the ceiling
OCCVM-L3

One light

Position is the full NOAA solar algorithm; response is the derivation of every surface quantity from it. One implementation, occvm/sundial.js, shared by every conforming tool — a second solar routine anywhere is the defect this law exists to prevent.

OCCVM-L4

Cast shadow

Depth is chosen; the offset is never authored. (--lx, --ly) points toward the sun, so a cast falls at −(lx, ly) and a lit bevel sits at +(lx, ly). Every fixed offset the spine replaced had this backwards, in both tools, and both read plausible.

cast-1
cast-2
cast-3
OCCVM-L5

Gilt is reserved

The gilt ramp marks what decides and nothing else. A surface that is merely important is not gilt; a number that settles something is. Malachite and ruby carry outcome, verdigris carries seam and age, bronze carries binding — none of them are interchangeable with this ramp.

OCCVM-L6

The mineral set

Closed, with fixed meanings: amethyst is the default field, malachite is affirmed/won/positive, ruby is negated/lost/failed. One implementation, occvm/minerals.js; each tool stores its own choice, and a tool may spend the mineral as widely or as narrowly as its own subject matter allows.

The picker is a specimen of L8 as much as of L6: a real <button>, 44px floor, aria-pressed in sync, the shared focus ring. It holds no state beyond this page view — a reference surface that remembered a choice would record a different golden frame depending on who looked at it last.

OCCVM-L7

Figure discipline

Numerals in a column are tabular, and no numeral that carries meaning depends on a face the visitor's operating system happens to supply. The face is IBM Plex Mono under the OFL, subset and embedded, in two real weights — a synthesised bold changes the advance width and breaks the column it sits in.

weight 4001,048,576.00
weight 6001,048,576.00
400−0.00071828
600−0.00071828

Both rows must align to the digit. If they do not, the face did not load and the browser is synthesising the weight — which is the exact failure L7 exists to prevent, and it is visible here without instrumentation.

OCCVM-L8

The interaction floor

Every action is a real control: correct element semantics, reachable by keyboard, state announced, a target of at least 44×44px, and one focus ring shared across the system. The floor exempts a target inline within a flow of text — WCAG 2.5.8's own carve-out, because a reading surface is a document rather than a control panel — and nothing that is chrome takes that exemption.

Specimen: the mineral picker above, the sweep below, and the row here. Tab through them — the ring is --gilt-b, 2px, offset 2px, and it is the same ring in both tools. Every target below is at or above the floor; the measured height is printed under each, read off the live box rather than asserted.

SPECIMENS

Every thickness, every scale

1.8's own brief: slabs at every thickness, controls in every state, ink at every scale. The states are above; the depths and the scale run here. A depth is chosen from the three the spine defines and never authored as an offset — these are the same three --occvm-cast-* values every surface in both tools picks from, and they all rake with the sun as you move the sweep.

Ink at every scale

Serif for prose and heads, mono for anything a column has to hold. Both faces answer to the same light: at night this whole block shifts with --bone and gains --nglow, and under a moon it recovers part of the way back toward its daylight value.

OCCVM-L9

Night

Night is a continuous quantity, not a state flag: --night ramps from 0 at −2° elevation to 1 at −10°. The civil / nautical / astronomical stages are additive over that ramp, not a replacement for it — --dusk-stage, at the standard boundaries. Night acts on ink only: no surface takes a glow.

Each cell is computed by calling the shared sundial at that elevation, not sampled from the clock, so the whole ramp is visible at once from any instant.

The sweep — dawn to night, on a slider rather than a clock

This is 1.8's own specified control, and it drives the whole page: every surface, bevel, cast and swatch above re-resolves as you move it, because they all read the same tokens the sundial is writing. Drag from one end to the other and the tool goes through its entire day in front of you. RESUME hands the page back to the real clock.

The moon is on this slider too, and it is the reason a reading taken at 21:40 differs from one at 23:10 at all — past −10° elevation --night is saturated and every other term is a function of it, so without a second light the two instants resolve identically. On a night when the moon is below the horizon at both, they still do, and that is a fact about the sky rather than a gap in the model.

OCCVM-L10

Vein habit

Veins are grown, not drawn — diffusion-limited aggregation, where a walker sticks the instant it touches the aggregate and branching is dendritic because a protruding tip screens the interior. Nobody authors the branching. Every stroke is a straight segment between a particle and the particle it stuck to; a fitted curve would be the bezier arriving back through the renderer.

Same seed, three habits. The mineral is aragonite — 2.0's anchor, one crystal for substrate and vein alike — so the growth radiates from a nucleation point and twins in threes, the pseudo-hexagonal cyclic twin aragonite is known for. --vein-habit is the anisotropy of that growth, and it lives in attachment, not travel: the walk is unbiased, and what differs by direction is whether a contact is accepted. Biasing the walker instead was measured and did nothing — a walker pushed outward leaves rather than sticking. At habit 0 attachment is indifferent to direction, which is exactly what an equant dendrite is.
